sentences.text: This meeting is being recorded.
Hi, Kaffir, can you hear me?
Hello, Angie.
Yes, I can.
How are you?
Good, thank you.
How you doing?
Very well, thanks a lot.
Whereabouts he calling from?
Tel Aviv.
Ah.
Have you been today?
I haven't, no.
We've got a few clients in Tel Aviv, funnily enough.
Oh, really?
Israel?
Really famous ones.
I don't know.
We just sold a company called Leaders Group.
Yeah, we just sold those.
Those guys at the end of last year.
So fairly well known influencer marketing agency.
Okay.
If you've heard of them.
Interesting.
We've just taken on a couple more clients as well.
Okay.
Yeah.
Nice.
It is nice.
It is nice.
How's things there?
Quiet today.
Yeah, you know, as usual, nothing special.
I mean, you know, business as usual.
Just getting started the new year and now people are getting back to hog.
Not now, but in the last, let's say two weeks, people are waking up.
Well, I think you have warmer weather than we have in the uk, but most likely.
I can understand that, but you have so many holidays.
That's not hard though.
Yeah, it's not hard.
It's not hard.
But you guys have a lot of days off.
You have more holidays than any other country.
I think that in Spain.
I think that in Spain they have more.
Yeah, I lived in Spain for almost four years and in Spain, I mean, not much more, but they do have more.
But yeah, here in Israel we do have a lot of holidays.
You're always celebrating something.
Not always.
You know, sometimes we are fighting also, so.
Well, there is a little war going on.
Whether it's fighting or celebrating, you know, there isn't nothing in the middle.
Well, hopefully we'll give you something to celebrate if we can work together.
So I don't know how much you know about capital a group.
We're happy to give you a little bit of a background.
So we're a marketing services M and A advisory.
So we just work with marketing agencies, media companies, those types of things.
And we work both on the buy and the sell side.
So we help buyers find agencies to acquire.
They can be larger agencies, agency groups or private equity.
And we work as well with agency owners who are looking to sell and exit their businesses as well.
We own and operate a platform called Agencies Co, which is a marketplace for agency owners to buy and sell agencies.
Over the last 12 months or so, we've probably done about 50 million in transactions.
So we, we tend to work at the sort of lower to lower end of the middle market.
So most agencies that we work with probably don't really go over about 20 or 30 million in revenue unless we're working on the buy side.
We work with some agency groups that are doing hundreds of millions in revenue as well.
But yeah, we get to see both sides of the table negotiating for buyers and sellers.
So it gives us a lot of insight into what deals do close.

Obviously the purpose of today's call is just to understand more about your business and your goals and see if there's a fit with our network and see if we can help you reach those goals and help you with your exit.
So be good to hear a little bit more about your business.
A to Z?
Yeah, we say A to Z in the uk but I'm just humoring you.
A to Z Digital.
So yeah, be good to know how you got started and what it is that you're looking to achieve.
So I've been in the business of, in the eco, in the e commerce business for 15 years, something like that.

And I started at a seller on Amazon and you know, along the years many businesses reached out to me, mostly here in Israel and you know, asked me how I do this and how can I improve my business or can I start an e commerce business, etc.
Etc.
And about two years ago, two and a half years ago, I decided to shut down the e commerce sales business.

I used to sell gun holsters because it wasn't profitable at all anymore and to be focused on the advisory side and you know, to be an agency and help other businesses to do whatever they want to do on online, not only on Amazon, you know, any, any kind of e commerce activity that they want to do I can help them with because this is something that I've done for many, many years to my own business when I used to sell online and, and now I'm working with a lot of climb, a lot, a lot.
I'm working with clients in the US mostly in the US and also here in Israel.
It's a retainer basis on, with most of them.
It depends on the scale and the size of the business and how much I need to invest in it, how much time I need to invest in it and then I'm, I'm pricing it according to that.
Right now I'm working with 12, with 12 clients and it's very, you know, depends on the time of the year and all that.
Sometimes I had also times that I had like 20 clients and then 15, 12, it depends, but let's say on average about 15.
And so that's about the business.
Most of the clients, most of them are selling on Amazon and I'm helping them with that.

And we are doing sometimes marketing on, on Amazon and sometimes off Amazon, which means influencer marketing, working with influencers to drive traffic to their Amazon stores or working, doing Google Ads or social media ads or social media content creation.
So we are doing that as well.
But most of them are coming from Amazon, you know, doing Amazon selling on Amazon.
And you know, I, I haven't, I never thought, I mean, I know I would love to sell if I could, you know, and see what we can do.
I'm not sure if this is the right time to do that.

I mean, it, you know, it caught my eye and I decided that, you know, let's speak and see and let's see, you know, what, what can we do if we can do and if we cannot do, how can we reach the point where we can sell the business?
Okay, so you're kind of just inquiring at the moment.
There's no sort of personal pressure or, or business reason to, to sell right now.
So in terms of the size of the company, what would you say that the business is doing now?
Sort ballpark revenue.
Revenue around, I would say about 20k a month, something like that.
Between 15 to 20.
Is that US dollars?
Yes.
And is the business profitable?
Yeah, it is.
Of course not.
Of course, but yes.
And how many people work in the business?
I'm working mostly with the freelancers.
Not mostly only with freelancers.
So it depends on the project.
You know, it depends on the clients.
So there isn't any employees on the, on the company to just yourself?
Yes.
Okay, still about 10, 40k.
Did you know what your profit margin is at the moment?
We'd say around 35, something like that.
Okay, and what are you looking for?
You know, what's, what's the goal for you?
You looking to take money off the table?
Do you want to retire and do something different or.
You know, I don't think that I can sell a business and retired.
I wish I could, but that's not the situation.
Not yet, at least.
Yeah, you know, I'm thinking about maybe going to a new direction, do something new with my life.
And this is why I'm thinking about that direction.
But so, yeah, mostly I would like to sell it and continue to my own way, to something new, do something, something new with my life.
Okay.
So a lot of people think that only large agencies sell, but actually small businesses do sell as well.
Small agencies.
We actually sold a company in Los Angeles last year and I think, I think their Their profits were zero, but their actual revenue was only a few hundred thousand.
But we had so many offers on it, it was probably one of the records.
Well, two reasons.
One was because it was in Los Angeles, so that got people excited.
Also it was performance marketing, which kind of everybody wants to get into.
And I would say there's probably an element of that, what you're doing.
But also the E commerce space is a very busy one and obviously Israel is kind of gateway to the Middle east as well.
So there's a lot of opportunity coming out of Israel and also there's a lot of talent in Israel, including the tech.
Yes, yeah.
So, you know, a lot of American and European companies are aware that they can tap into that talent as well.
So I think there's potentially a lot of interest.
And also I think one of the, the reasons why we, we sold one of the last agencies from Israel quite quickly is because the buyers CEO was Jewish as well.
So I think American guy and I think he was, he was keen to make an acquisition in Israel.
So there's obviously that reason as well.

So I think it's possibly a better opportunity than maybe you, you initially think you're probably thinking it's a bit small, you're not sure whether it's going to generate enough of an opportunity for you.
Roughly, I would say just a quick calculation.
The business is possibly worth about a 3x on your EBITDA, your profit margin.
So you know, it's a, an easy, easy one to work out, but roughly about a quarter of a million dollars, possibly maybe a little bit more.
It really does depend if we can get people excited and they want to make a strong offer.
But generally speaking, smaller agencies around this size are usually around a 3x and they are easy to fund.
I'm sure you've got this scheme in Israel as well, but they have it in the US where it's called a small business loan from the SBA or Small Business Association.
Yes.
And they're easy to get, but they are also not very adventurous in terms of the valuations they give to those businesses.
They're usually somewhere around a three or four times margin.
But what they do mean is they offer business owners or all of the cash to buy out another business.
So it's quite straightforward.
I know they do have them across Europe as well as the us but they don't have them in the uk, funnily enough.
Okay.

But it does make the process quite straightforward, particularly for these smaller transactions, because it just means somebody Else who maybe either runs an agency or has been part of an agency would like to buy a company.
It makes it quite straightforward for them to make these small, small transactions.
So in terms of what you want, what's your timeline at the moment?
Does that sound exciting or are you just thinking, you know, I'm gonna keep my head down for another two or three years, grow the business.
No, actually that sounds quite, quite nice.
I mean, if, if we will be able to move forward with that, that can be an option.
Completely an option.
Sounds fair, sounds like a fair offer.
And if there will be anything relevant, I would love to hear about it.
Yeah, so I mean it's quite straightforward process from us.
So as I mentioned, the platform that we have, Agencies Co, is completely free to list on the platform.
We do take 5% on the transaction for transactions over 1 million.
Obviously this is a smaller one, so we take 10%.
But it's, it's quite an easy process.
I can either sign you up now or I can send you this, this form.
I'll just share it with you.
Let's have a look.

So I can send you this if you don't have time now, but basically it's just your, your basic details, details of the agency address, a little bit of general information, what it is that you guys do and the opportunity, obviously you can make it sound a bit more sexy.
This does tend to fill itself out.
So once you start typing, a lot of it will fill itself out and then just select what type of agency is.

This is the tough bit I think is just, is being able to come up with the percentages of project work and retainer work and then obviously the listing price and the multiple, as I've said, it's probably going to go for a 3x on, on the 35%, so fairly straightforward.
And then just the revenue for the last three years, the EBITDA for the last three years, the revenue, yeah, industry served, services that you provide.
You can add more as you go along.
Some people just put in three years, but you put in more and that's it.
Sign yourself away, submit the listing and then we'll get that on our back end.
Like I say, there's, there's no charge to list, but we will produce an engagement, a full engagement letter just to make sure we've got you signed up if we find a buyer.
And then once we're listed, that gets sent out 20,000 people on our mailing list.
And those are agency owners, agency buyers of all different types.
Some of those are, like I said, sort of private owner operators that are looking to make acquisitions.
But also my team, we have a seasoned M and A team, they also search, do sort of outreach on their own personal networks as well.
And if we find a buyer that M A team then just steps in.
You know, you can absolutely rely on them from start to finish of getting the deal negotiated and closed.
So.
Yeah, all right.
Pretty pain free process.
Yeah, sounds good.
So I will sign up later on and let's take it from there.
Let's see.
Okay, I'm going to send you this link and as soon as we get that form filled out, it starts the process and obviously we've got a lot of automations in the back end that just start ticking along.
So yeah, that's it.
Okay.
Okay.
Or if you, if you're, if you're happy with that, then obviously we can get started straight away.
It usually takes about six months to get a business sold start to finish.
So for us.
Yeah, or no rush.
Yeah.
But you can expect to be sipping cocktails around July, August.
Sounds good, Andy.
Okay, brilliant.
All right, fair.
Nice to meet you.
I'll send you via email as soon as I get off the call.
All right, working with you.
Thanks a lot.
All right, cheers.
Have a great.
Thanks, you too.
Bye.
Bye.
They're recording.

summary.action_items:
**Kfir Abud**
Fill out the listing form for A to Z Digital on Agencies Co platform (17:23)

**Andy Day**
Send the listing form link to Kfir via email (17:38)
summary.overview: In the exploratory sales meeting, Kfir Abud and Andy Day discussed potential collaboration regarding Kfir's e-commerce advisory business, A to Z Digital, which Kfir is considering selling. Kfir provided an overview of his business, noting its focus on advisory services in the e-commerce sector, a profitable monthly revenue of $15-20k with a 35% profit margin, and an estimated business value of $250,000. Andy, representing Capital A Group, explained their role in facilitating agency transactions, detailing their commission structure and the listing process on their platform, Agencies Co. Kfir expressed a keen interest in selling, and the meeting concluded with action items for Kfir to fill out the listing form and for Andy to send the link.
summary.short_summary: In an exploratory sales meeting, Kfir Abud from A to Z Digital outlined his e-commerce advisory business, which has been operational for about 2.5 years and generates $15-20k monthly with a 35% profit margin. Kfir, who primarily serves clients in the US and Israel, is interested in selling his business valued at approximately $250,000. Andy Day from Capital A Group explained their role in facilitating agency transactions, highlighting their commission structure and listing process on their platform, Agencies Co. The meeting concluded with action items for Kfir to complete the listing form and Andy to send the necessary link to proceed with the sale.
